subject: System Design
title: ACID Properties
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: ACID Properties.

hook.text: You transfer $500 between accounts. The debit succeeds but the credit fails. Where did the money go?

buildup.text: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the four guarantees of reliable transactions.

discovery.text: Atomicity ensures both debit and credit succeed or both fail. No partial transfers, ever.

twist.text: ACID transactions are expensive. They require locks and coordination that limit throughput.

climax.text: Relational databases offer ACID by default. Most NoSQL databases sacrifice some of these guarantees for speed.

punchline.text: ACID ensures all-or-nothing: no partial failures.

quiz.question: What does Atomicity in ACID guarantee?
options: All operations in a transaction succeed or all fail
